newsitem.title: USA: Sears margin up, expenses down, credit strong.
newsitem.headline: Sears margin up, expenses down, credit strong.

text.p: Sears, Roebuck and Co., which earlier reported record third-quarter earnings, said swift business at its stores and credit card operation and higher margins fueled the strong results.
Domestic gross margins as a percent of merchandising sales and services rose to 26.1 percent in the third quarter from 25.6 percent during the same period last year, Sears said.

"Customers have responded enthusiastically to our department store renovations, broader assortments and quality brands, especially in apparel, and are heavily shopping our off-the-mall stores," said Sears Chairman Arthur Martinez.
"Our excellent revenue growth, improved domestic gross margins and strong credit business led to record third-quarter earnings," Martinez said.

Earlier, Sears said it earned $279 million, or $0.68 a share, during the third quarter versus $228 million, or $0.56 a share, in the same period of 1995. This year's income included a pre-tax charge of $17 million for a restructuring at Sears Canada.
The results were ahead of Wall Street's expectations of earnings of $0.64 a share in the third quarter, according to First Call.
The retailer's total revenues rose 7.4 percent to $9.07 billion in the third quarter from $8.44 billion a year ago.

At the company's domestic operations, income rose 24.3 percent to $292 million, and revenue rose 8.4 percent to $8.28 billion in the third quarter, fueled by gains at the credit card operation and sales at its department stores.

Sears increased its provision for uncollectable credit card accounts, due to growth in the credit receivables portfolio as well as increased delinquencies and personal bankruptcies, the retailer said.

The company did not disclose by how much it increased the provision, but it was the second quarter in a row that costs for bad credit card debt had risen. During the second quarter, Sears increased its provision for uncollectable accounts to $254 million from $147 million in the second quarter of 1995.

Still, Sears said the credit card operation's revenues were up 19 percent, reflecting higher receivable balances resulting from strong merchandise sales and the impact of uniform pricing. The improved credit revenues and reduced funding rates improved net interest margin.
Sears' department store operations, about half of which have undergone remodelings, also posted a strong revenue gain, up seven percent.

"The outstanding performance of our department stores during the third quarter and first nine months is a credit to the hard work of our associates, and shows the progress we've made in revitalizing our mall-based business," Martinez said.
International operations, including Sears' merchandising and credit operations in Canada and Mexico, lost $13 million versus a loss of $7 million in the third quarter of 1995.
